children: West African crude differentials were higher than expected, traders said on Monday, which was weighing on demand.
Crude differentials were too high, a trader said, leading to market players being in wait-and-watch mode despite freight rates easing slightly.
Price reporting agencies were reporting Nigerian grades such as Bonga and Forcados being at around plus $6 to dated Brent for October, he said.
Two other traders also noted that the prices were too high and a fair value would be when differentials were a dollar or two lower.
A crude tender issued by Nigeria's Dangote refinery was closing, the results of which would be announced tomorrow.
Last week, traders had said that there were still September cargoes of Angolan and Nigerian crude available.
In the wider market, Japan's crude oil imports rose 17% in July, with imports from Africa rising around 27% compared to last year.
